message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to buy or auction the property at MARVIN_GARDENS.

I have $426 and own the red properties. The opponent has the other reds and light blues with hotels. I am weighing whether to buy this property or auction it.

The red group contains only three properties. The opponent owns the other two reds and the light blues with hotels.

The opponent owns Indiana, Tennessee, and Pennsylvania Avenue. Indiana is the red property I lack. The other players hold Baltic, Electric Company, Atlantic and Ventnor, Water Works, Park Place, Boardwalk, and the railroads.

Buying Marvin Gardens would leave me with $146. It would also block the opponent from completing the yellow monopoly. The cash situation is risky.

I am calculating the rent values of the opponent's properties. The pink monopoly with three houses yields $450 to $500 per visit. The light blue hotels pay $550 to $600 each. The dark blue properties pay $1100 to $1400.

Boardwalk with three houses pays $1400. That is fatal. I cannot survive landing there even if I mortgage my red properties for about $230.

Mortgaging my red properties would leave only $376 liquid. That is still short of the $450 to $500 rent from the pink monopoly with three houses. I cannot afford a pink landing without raising more cash. I own no other properties to mortgage.

Even with the full $656 liquid from mortgaging my red properties, I cannot afford a pink three-house rent. Virginia Avenue would cost $500, which exceeds the available cash. Boardwalk with three houses remains impossible to pay regardless.

I should auction Marvin Gardens rather than buy it. The bankruptcy risk from the pink monopoly is too high. Blocking the yellow set would be strategic, but p3 already owns two yellows and could build houses there. They have $293 in cash, while p4 has only $14 and p1 is in jail with $57. I will auction to avoid the financial danger.

I will auction to preserve cash for the rent storm. I am weighing whether to encourage p1 and p4 to bid, since they have little money and cannot outbid p3.

I cannot bid in the auction myself. I must choose between buying now or starting an auction. If I start an auction, p3 will likely outbid me to complete the yellow monopoly. The other players have almost no cash and cannot meaningfully raise the price.

I rechecked the mortgage math. Keeping the property leaves $426 cash. Mortgaging one red property yields $536, enough to pay a $450 pink rent and leave $86. Mortgaging both reds yields $656, covering the $500 Virginia rent with $156 left. The light blue hotels and Park Place are also manageable. I can survive these hits without buying.

I am now planning my next moves. After this turn I will pass Water Works, Ventnor, Short Line, and Park Place. Pacific and NC are mortgaged, so they will not collect rent.
